evidence: src/application/use-cases/AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts, CancelOrderUseCase.ts and GetOrderUseCase.ts all look up the order with requireOrder(this.orders, orderId). None repeats the not-found check.
src/application/use-cases/AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts and ListOrdersByStateUseCase.ts both convert the status string with parseOrderStatus from domain/order/OrderStatus.

src/application/use-cases/PlaceOrderUseCase.ts calls this.stock.reserve(order.lines) and CancelOrderUseCase.ts calls this.stock.release(order.lines). Stock is handled only through StockReservationService.
Every use case returns its result through a DTO mapper: toOrderDto in five of them and toStockLevelDto in ListStockLevelsUseCase.ts.

src/application/use-cases/AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts state changes go through order.advanceTo(target). The 'cancelled' guard only routes callers to CancelOrderUseCase and does not copy the transition rules.
src/application/use-cases/ListStockLevelsUseCase.ts follows the same constructor-injection pattern with execute() and products.findAll().map(toStockLevelDto).
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module holds only application use cases. Each is a class with one `execute` method that takes its dependencies through the constructor and returns DTOs. They all follow the same pattern: load or create through a repository, call domain behaviour, save, then map with a DTO mapper.

The module's shared abstractions are used consistently:
- Every single-order lookup goes through `requireOrder`, so no file repeats its own not-found check.
- Both places that read an order status string use `parseOrderStatus`.
- Stock reservation and release go only through `StockReservationService`.
- DTO mapping goes only through `toOrderDto` and `toStockLevelDto`.

`ListStockLevelsUseCase` reads products rather than orders. It still fits the module's role as the application-layer entry points the controllers call, so it is not an unrelated concern.

In `AdvanceOrderUseCase`, the rejection of a `cancelled` target sends callers to the cancel operation. It is not a copy of the order's transition rules, which stay in `order.advanceTo`. I found no duplicated rule and no bypassed abstraction.
